datasets.annotation_method: Native speaker translation from standard Hindi sentences created by domain experts, followed by expert validation. Multi-class labels are dialect names assigned to each sentence.

data_creator_info.creator_affiliation: Indian Institute of Technology Mandi; Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur
data_creator_info.evidence: We recruit 23 annotators (2 per dialect, and 1 for Odia) and 11 experts (1 per dialect) from the specific regions where these dialects are spoken. All annotators are compensated for their linguistic expertise at a rate exceeding the local minimum wage.

datasets.notes: Derived from the INDIC-DIALECT parallel corpus. Sentences from all 11 dialects compiled with dialect names as ground-truth labels. Classification is over 11 dialect classes, not the 2 standard languages.

datasets.annotation_method: Dialect sentences serve as questions; correct answer is the parallel standard language translation from the corpus. Three hard distractors are semantically similar near-misses created using the approach from Zellers et al. 2019.

data_creator_info.creator_affiliation: Indian Institute of Technology Mandi; Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur
data_creator_info.evidence: We recruit 23 annotators (2 per dialect, and 1 for Odia) and 11 experts (1 per dialect) from the specific regions where these dialects are spoken. All annotators are compensated for their linguistic expertise at a rate exceeding the local minimum wage.

datasets.notes: Derived from the INDIC-DIALECT parallel corpus. Presents a dialect sentence with four candidate interpretations in the standard language (one correct translation, three hard distractors).

datasets.annotation_method: Human translation by native speakers with expert validation. Inter-annotator agreement (Cohen's Kappa) of 0.89 on 5% subset. Parallel corpus formatted as source-target sentence pairs supporting both dialect-to-language and language-to-dialect translation.

data_creator_info.creator_affiliation: Indian Institute of Technology Mandi; Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur
data_creator_info.evidence: We recruit 23 annotators (2 per dialect, and 1 for Odia) and 11 experts (1 per dialect) from the specific regions where these dialects are spoken. All annotators are compensated for their linguistic expertise at a rate exceeding the local minimum wage.

datasets.notes: Derived from the INDIC-DIALECT parallel corpus (13,000 sentence pairs). Supports bidirectional translation: dialect-to-standard-language and standard-language-to-dialect. 70:30 train:test split used in experiments.
